questions.q: What do Loehr and Schwartz argue is more crucial than time for high performance?
questions.why: They claim managing energy, not time, leads to better outcomes.

questions.q: Which type of energy is described as the most important because it depends on sleep, diet, and exercise?
questions.why: Physical energy is linked to sleep, nutrition, and activity.

questions.q: How many sources of energy do the authors identify?
questions.why: The book lists physical, emotional, mental, and spiritual energy.

questions.q: What is the suggested benefit of accepting criticism at work, according to the text?
questions.why: Accepting criticism avoids expensive long‑term consequences.

questions.q: If a day were 100 hours long, what would still limit what you can accomplish?
questions.why: Even with unlimited time, lack of energy would be the constraint.
